title: api: schema versioning, beta headers, and backward-compat shims for streaming & OpenAI compatibility
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation: We need an explicit API request/response schema versioning mechanism to safely evolve streaming frame formats, function/tool-calling payloads, and structured output while preserving the OpenAI-compat layer for existing customers. This PR introduces a lightweight versioning header, beta opt-in header, server-side backward-compatibility shims for older client formats, and deprecation warnings for fields slated for removal.

Summary of changes: added X-Redwood-API-Version header (default v1); added X-Redwood-Beta header to opt into experimental schema changes (v2+); implemented server-side shims that translate legacy request/response fields to the new schema; updated OpenAI-compat layer to accept both legacy and v2 streaming chunk/frame formats; deprecation warnings surfaced in response headers and in the dashboard logs; docs and migration guide.

Checklist:
- [x] Add header parsing and version routing in api-gateway and openai-compat middleware
- [x] Implement v2 streaming frame format support and server-side shim to accept legacy frames
- [x] Introduce deprecation warnings (response header + event to audit-log)
- [x] Add feature flag to gate behavior during rollout
- [x] Update unit/integration tests and add streaming e2e test variants
- [x] Update docs, migration guide, and release notes

Behavior notes for engineers:
- Default behavior remains v1 unless caller sends X-Redwood-API-Version: v2 or X-Redwood-Beta: 1.0. Clients using the OpenAI-compat endpoint without headers will continue to receive v1-shaped responses.
- When X-Redwood-Beta is present, the gateway will accept and return v2 payload shapes (structured output ABI tweaks, new function_call metadata, and streaming frame envelopes).
- Server-side shims accept legacy fields (e.g., top-level model_config -> model_settings) and emit deprecation warnings in the X-Redwood-Deprecation header with a Linear ref. Shims are logged to audit-log with reason and source_client.

Impact & rollout: This PR is designed to be safe-by-default. We will gate the beta behavior behind a feature flag and enable it for internal traffic first, then opt-in customers. Backward-compat shims are intended as temporary (6 months) and will be removed per ENG-2104.

References: Linear ENG-2104, ENG-2110. Related PRs: openai-compat follow-ups scheduled next sprint.

release_notes:
- Introduced API versioning header X-Redwood-API-Version (v1 default, v2 opt-in)
- Added X-Redwood-Beta header for experimental schema opt-in
- Backward-compat shims for v1 -> v2 translation (temporary, 6 month window)
- Deprecation warnings surfaced via X-Redwood-Deprecation header and audit logs
- OpenAI-compat updated to accept legacy and v2 streaming formats
migration_notes: Short migration guide: 1) If you rely on the current OpenAI-compat behavior, no changes required immediately. 2) To opt into new structured output and streaming frames, send X-Redwood-Beta: 1.0 or X-Redwood-API-Version: v2 in requests. 3) Update any code reading top-level model_config to use model_settings; the shim will map model_config -> model_settings and add a deprecation header. 4) For streaming consumers: prefer parsing by frame_type; v2 frames include frame_type and seq_id. 5) Monitor X-Redwood-Deprecation headers and the migration dashboard.
notes_for_release_eng: Rollout plan: enable feature flag for internal traffic (canary) for 48h, monitor stream stability metrics and audit-log volume, then enable for opt-in customers. Plan to remove shims after 6 months if migration metrics show <5% legacy traffic (ENG-2104).
security_considerations: No new auth surface. We add additional header parsing; validated with input sanitizer. Audit logger will rate-limit shim warnings to avoid information disclosure via logs.
observability_changes: Added metrics: api_version_requests{version=v1|v2}, shim_translations_total, shim_translation_errors, deprecation_header_emitted_total. Updated per-route dashboards to show schema mix and migration progress.
